question: price the per-forward device program-cache clear+rebuild at tt_bio/boltz2.py:5731, and ship it if it wins

lever.added_by: 8859d7e1, 'to avoid stale program-cache state across variable-shape sweeps'
lever.candidate_default: keep the cache; clear only on a shape change, or not at all

band_basis: c12-host-decomp measured the clear+enable CALL at 0.0174 s for two cycles at both 1350 and 800 MHz, i.e. 0.0087 s per forward and clock-immune. That is the floor of what the flag can return.
c12-host-decomp's one clean 1350 MHz rep read 0.0524 s (bare 14.9207 s vs keepcache 14.8683 s). One rep per arm, so no spread to score it against: UNRESOLVED, not 0.0524 s.
the band top of 0.20 s is 4x that single rep, not the 2.3 s the brief inherited.

band_top_retracted.inherited: 0.0-2.3 s, from perf/boltz2-affinity-fixedcost screen_walls.txt at 256 aa: structure 15.1 s with the clear vs 12.8 s with it suppressed
band_top_retracted.why_retracted: that screen's 2.3 s exceeds the ENTIRE measured non-device remainder of a 512 aa fold (1.6489-1.6720 s, c12-profiled-fold), and a program-cache rebuild is host program assembly plus a binary write, not 2.3 s of it. The same screen's cold first target moved 27.7 -> 13.7 s, which cannot be a clear-vs-no-clear effect on a cold cache, so its warm figure is not trusted either.
band_top_retracted.carried_forward_as: an explicit falsifier: if this row measures anything above 0.20 s, the inherited screen was right and the retraction was wrong. Recorded so the retraction is scored, not assumed.

what_would_make_it_negative: a FULL program cache makes every op's cache LOOKUP dearer -- the hit path hashes the operand specs against N resident entries, where the cleared arm probes a table that starts empty and grows through the fold. If lookup cost scales with occupancy, keepcache pays on every op while bare pays only on the misses.
programs that persist hold their L1/DRAM program buffers, so the keepcache arm runs the fold's tensor allocations against a more fragmented heap.
the effect is the same order as the session noise floor, so a single rep can land either sign -- which is exactly what c12 saw at 800 MHz (-0.4154 s, keepcache reps spanning 0.9486 s).
mass_filter_tier: 0.05 s -- 'building a lever whose mechanism is KNOWN'. The mechanism is a measured flag that already exists in production code and the build cost is flipping one default, so the 0.3 s speculative tier does not apply.

protocol.harness: perf/c12_host_decomp/decomp.py, reused not forked (holder parameterized, A/A arm and program-cache census added)
protocol.arms: bare / bare2 / keepcache -- bare2 is bare under a second label, an explicit A/A pair measured in the same session
protocol.interleaving: arms interleaved rep by rep AND the arm order rotated per rep, so a monotone drift inside a rep cannot land on one arm
protocol.why_interleaving_is_valid_here: the clear runs at the START of forward. A bare fold clears, then rebuilds, then leaves a FULL cache. The keepcache fold that follows it therefore hits every program it needs. So the bare-minus-keepcache delta is the rebuild, and the one-warm-process interleave is the most favourable protocol this lever can get.
protocol.clock: 1350 MHz forced through ARC FORCE_AICLK before every label and sampled at ~1 kHz DURING each fold; min=max=target required or the label is rejected
protocol.fixture: perf/size512/fixtures/cdk2x2_512, 200 sampling steps, 3 recycles, 1 sample, seed 0, no templates
protocol.pair: node 3, sibling node 2 verified idle by perf/c12_orchestrator/pair_guard/pair_idle.py before the read

instrument_control.flag_witness: env_flag is wrapped, so every label records which BRANCH ran rather than which environment was requested. A label whose queries disagree with its arm is a hard error.
instrument_control.cache_census: dev.num_program_cache_entries() after every fold. A bare fold and a keepcache fold must leave the SAME count; if they do not, the arms are not folding the same graph and the delta is not a rebuild.
instrument_control.known_answer: a bare fold's count taken immediately after the fold is the number of distinct programs a rebuild rebuilds. delta_s divided by that count is the per-program cost, and it has to be plausible host work (order 0.1-1 ms), not 10 ms.

correctness_registered_before_running.why_it_is_not_free: 8859d7e1 added the clear deliberately. The risk case is the SECOND fold in one process on a DIFFERENT-sized target, which is what the platform worker loop does.
correctness_registered_before_running.firing_test_not_a_grep: ttnn exposes set_program_cache_misses_allowed(False). Fold target A, forbid misses, re-fold A: no throw proves every program hit. Then fold a different-sized target B with misses still forbidden: it MUST throw, which proves new shapes take NEW cache keys instead of silently reusing A's programs.
correctness_registered_before_running.digest_test: one process, sequence 512 -> 298 -> 512 -> 256 with KEEP=1, every CIF digest and plddt compared against the same sequence run with the production clear. A cache change must not move a digest at all, so bit-exactness IS the cheap check here and it is taken.
correctness_registered_before_running.kill_condition: any digest difference, or a miss-forbidden re-fold of the same target that throws
